battle.name: 始州之戰
battle.brief: 大象二年九月，益州人李嚴聚眾為亂，北周朝廷命隨國公楊堅率兵入蜀討之。官軍由漢中出劍門，前鋒抵利州、進逼始州。始州控蜀北咽喉，叛軍據城拒守，官軍以弩手壓住城頭、封死谷道，步騎乘隙反擊，潰其主力，叛首西走。卡面的秦弩在此扮演主角：弩機存力、連發不斷，正是仰攻劍門、封鎖谷口合用的兵器。

kit.name: 秦弩
kit.history: 弩機把拉力存起來，射速遠勝拉弓。守城的一方靠它把攻城的人壓在牆外。

countries: 大象二年（五百八十）秋，戰場落在北周最難抵達的西南一隅：梁州與益州交界的劍門關外，隸屬益州的利州、始州一線，山道狹窄，沱水自北而南穿谷而過，兩側山壁幾乎夾住通道。交戰的一方是北周朝廷與其徵發的關隴、荊襄兵馬：靜帝宇文闍在位，朝政盡歸丞相隋國公楊堅之手，軍力倚賴關隴世族八柱國、十二大將留下的部曲，朝廷自隴右、河洛、江漢分道出師，糧秣則取漢中屯田與劍南郡縣的賦斂。另一方是益州本地聚眾為亂的叛軍，據成都、窺梁益，靠山川險固自守，招募蜀中流民與本地部曲，器械自製、糧秣就地，人數眾而編制散。叛軍的後方是成都平原的稻米與蜀道物資，官軍的弱點恰恰是長途入蜀的糧道。兩軍在始州、劍門之間的窄谷裡比的不是兵力多寡，而是誰能把弩陣、步騎與漕船編成一條不斷的線。官軍內部還混編著北周宿衛舊部與新歸附的益州降兵，號令、行軍序列與賞罰都要靠楊堅一件件立起來，蜀道本身就成了考驗新接管者能否駕馭關隴軍制的場所。
countriesEn: In the autumn of AD 580, the second year of the Daxiang era, the battlefield lay in the southwest corner of Northern Zhou, the hardest of all to reach: outside Jianmen Pass, where Liangzhou met Yizhou, on the line of Lizhou and Shizhou in Yizhou, where the mountain track is narrow and the Tuo River cuts south through the gorge with the cliff walls closing in on both sides. One side was the Zhou court together with the columns it levied in Guanzhong, Jingxiang and the riverlands: the child emperor Yuwen Jue sat on the throne while real power lay with Chancellor Yang Jian, Duke of Sui, and the army rested on the hereditary military households left by the eight Pillars of State and the Twelve Generals of the Guanzhong clans, the court sending columns out from Longyou, Luoyang and Jianghan, drawing grain from the tuntian of Hanzhong and the taxes of the Jiannan commanderies. The other side was the rebel mass raised in Yizhou itself, which seized Chengdu and threatened Liang and Yi, holding the mountain gorges as its shield, enrolling the displaced people of Shu and the local war-bands, making its own weapons and living off its own grain. The rebels' strength lay behind them, in the rice of the Chengdu plain and the goods that moved along the Shu roads, while the court's true weakness was the long line of supply into Shu. What the two sides measured against each other in the narrow gorge between Shizhou and Jianmen was therefore not the mass of numbers but who could stitch the crossbow line, the foot and horse, and the river transport into one unbroken chain. On the court side the old Zhou guard was still mixed in with newly submitted troops from Yizhou, so the march order, the sequence of columns and the system of rewards all had to be built by Yang Jian from scratch; the road into Shu itself became the test of whether the newcomer could handle the Guanzhong military system.
people: 這場戰役的樞紐人物是尚未稱帝的楊堅。他以隋國公、丞相主持北周軍政，四月平定鄴城的尉遲迥之後威權更重，九月再度領兵入蜀，把一次地方叛亂變成北周末年最具象徵意味的西南遠征；他選擇的路線決定了這場仗怎麼打。益州叛首李嚴在《隋書》等傳記中被記為聚眾為亂的首領，其生平與結局諸說並存，或云敗後請降，或云西走為流寇，史無定論，記錄相當疏略。益州刺史一級的守臣在叛亂中不能守成都，退保諸郡，其姓名與行止各書記載不一，也難以一一對證。官軍方面的將校姓名、編制與分道兵數，傳記同樣闕漏，只能知道楊堅親將主力出劍門，另遣別將守漢中、護漕運，穩住後方。蜀中豪右與獠部首領的取態亦不一致：有人響應叛軍以爭地盤，有人閉門自守以保鄉里，日後隋朝設官置吏、重新編戶，正是要收拾這批地方勢力。陳朝此時正逢宣帝新喪、太子初立的混亂，蜀中流亡南下的舊戶既被叛軍裹挾，也讓南朝在川西多了一線不完全可靠的指望。
peopleEn: The pivot of this campaign was Yang Jian, who was not yet emperor. As Duke of Sui and Chancellor he directed the military government of Northern Zhou, and after crushing Wei Chi-chiong at Yecheng in April his authority was greater than ever; in September he led an army into Shu once more, turning a local rising into the most emblematic of the far-western expeditions of late Zhou, and the route he chose decided how the war would be fought. The rebel leader in Yizhou is recorded in the histories, the Sui shu among them, as Li Yan, who raised a mass of men; his life and his end are variously reported, some saying he surrendered after his defeat, others that he fled west as a bandit, and there is no settled account, the record being very thin. The governor of Yizhou could not hold Chengdu once the rising began and fell back on the other commanderies; his name and his movements differ from book to book and cannot be checked one by one. The names of the commanders, the organisation and the number of men sent down each road are just as poorly recorded: all that can be said is that Yang Jian took the main body through Jianmen himself and posted other officers to guard Hanzhong and escort the river transport so as to steady the rear. The local great families and the chiefs of the mountain peoples were divided in their response: some joined the rebels to win ground for themselves, others shut their gates and held fast to keep their own villages safe, and the later Sui establishment of officials and a fresh registration of households was aimed at settling exactly these local powers. Meanwhile the Chen court was in confusion after the death of Emperor Xuan and the accession of the crown prince, and the old households of Shu who had fled south were both swept up by the rebels and gave the southern court one more unreliable hope on the far western frontier.
kits: 卡面這件秦弩，是這場山地攻防的真正主角。弩機把拉力先存起來，射手不必臨陣拉滿弓臂，便能以比角弓更整、更有殺傷力的箭矢射擊；魏晉南北朝的蜀地郡縣普遍置備弩具，甲士持強弩、縣兵持蹶張弩，是當時常見的配給方式之一。蜀中弩法另有來歷：秦人入蜀、楚人據峽，弓弩之技本地原有根基，漢時巴郡叟族與犍為一帶的部曲皆以善射著稱，三國蜀漢記載裡的元戎連弩與木牛流馬，更把弩與山地運輸綁在一起，說明蜀人很早便懂得用機械彌補山路之難。作戰中，弩兵被配置在劍門谷道兩側的高地與坡塬，一列列用蹶張法張弦待發，射程百步上下至二百步；強弩與石弩架在木構弩臺上，居高臨下射壓城頭與谷道，把出城的敵騎壓在開闊處，使守方步卒無法展開。步弓手在弩陣側翼輪替前進，補上弩手裝填的空隙，箭鏃兼取秦漢以來的金屬箭首與魏晉常用的三角形鋼鏃，穿透皮甲綻甲。攻城一面，官軍備有撞車、雲梯、巢車與投石砲；糧秣方面，漢中屯田所出沿嘉陵江轉入沱水以舟船運抵成都平原，關中河洛的粟麥則靠車牛沿金牛道北運，人力牛力都在谷道裡耗損，馬匹仰河西與吐谷渾供給。除兵器之外，蜀地城防所用的木構望樓、拒馬與陷坑，也是這場仗裡常見的器物。
kitsEn: The piece on the card, the Chinese crossbow, is the true protagonist of this mountain fight. The lock stores the draw first, so the shooter does not have to pull a bow to full bend at the moment of release, and can send a shaft far straighter and far more killing than an ordinary recurve; in Wei, Jin and the Northern and Southern dynasties crossbows were kept in general supply in the commanderies of Shu, with armoured men holding strong crossbows and the militia holding the hand-worked treading type, one of the commonest patterns of issue of the age. The crossbow in Shu had a pedigree of its own: Qin colonists and Chu occupants brought the craft into the region, the archery of the Ba commandery and the war-bands around Qianwei were already famous for shooting in Han times, and the records of Shu-Han in the Three Kingdoms speak of the repeating crossbow and the wooden ox and gliding horse, binding the crossbow to the transport problem of the mountain roads and showing that the people of Shu had long used machines to make up for the difficulty of the terrain. In the fighting, crossbowmen were posted on the heights and slopes on both sides of the Jianmen gorge, file after file cocking their weapons by the treading method and waiting, with an effective range of a hundred paces and up to two hundred; heavy crossbows and stone-thrown engines were mounted on timber platforms to shoot down from above onto the city walls and the road, holding the enemy horse out in the open where a defending foot could not deploy. Bowmen worked forward along the flanks of the crossbow line in relief, filling the interval while the crossbowmen reset, and the heads were drawn both from the metal arrowheads of Qin and Han and from the triangular steel points in common use in Wei and Jin, piercing leather and splitting armour. On the side of the assault the court brought up battering rams, scaling ladders, observation towers and stone-throwing engines, and for supply the grain of the Hanzhong tuntian was carried down the Jialing and turned into the Tuo for river transport to the Chengdu plain, while the millet and wheat of Guanzhong and Luoyang were hauled north by cart and ox along the Jinniu road, man-power and oxen both being consumed in the gorges, with horses drawn from Hexi and from the Tuyuhun. Alongside the weapons, the timber watch-towers, caltrops and pits of Shu fortification were familiar objects in this campaign as well.
tactics: 劍門關一線的地形決定了打法：谷道兩側山壁陡立，車戰無用，騎兵不能展開，攻城方必須先奪取制高點，把弓弩壓在谷口，再以步卒挾長槊、大盾列陣前行。楊堅入蜀的部署是先安後方：留兵守漢中，護住沱水漕運與金牛道，再督率主力出劍門，進逼利州、始州。接戰之後，官軍在始州以東的高地布列弩陣，弓弩覆蓋城頭與郊野通道，叛軍若出城反擊，便要在弩雨之下行進上百步，往往還未與官軍步卒接觸即已潰散；官軍再以步騎乘隙逼近城根，逼守軍收縮，同時分兵繞趨山谷兩側的隘口，切斷叛軍往成都與北面的連絡。糧道是攻守的真正命脈：官軍不急於強攻，而以弩兵封鎖谷道、以騎兵巡截糧道，逼叛軍在城內耗盡存糧；叛軍則試圖以遊騎出城焚燒官軍糧車、襲擊漢中，以拖延。招撫與軍事壓力並行：叛軍內部有地方豪右與流民的不同利益，官軍一面續以弩兵施加壓力，一面使人傳話曉諭，說明歸順可保鄉里、拒守則城破之後無生路，最終叛軍主力在始州線上崩潰，餘眾散入山林，官軍得以順利進軍成都。整場戰役的節奏，與其說是一次攻城對決，不如說是弩陣、封鎖與斷糧三件事合力把對手逼到無處可守。
tacticsEn: The ground along Jianmen decided how the war was fought: the cliff walls on either side of the gorge left no room for chariot action and no space for horse to deploy, so the side attacking had first to seize the heights, press the bows and crossbows down on the mouth of the pass, and only then advance with foot soldiers carrying long spears and large shields in line. Yang Jian's plan on entering Shu was to settle the rear first: he left troops to hold Hanzhong and guard the river transport on the Tuo and the Jinniu road, and only then led the main body through Jianmen to press on Lizhou and Shizhou. Once in contact, the court deployed its crossbow line on the heights east of Shizhou, so that bows covered the city walls and the approaches through the open country; any rebel sortie had to cross a hundred paces under a rain of bolts and often broke up before it could even reach the court infantry. The foot and horse then closed in to the foot of the walls, forcing the defenders to draw back, while detached columns worked round the passes on both flanks of the valley to cut the rebels off from Chengdu and from the north. The supply line was the true life of the campaign: the court did not hurry into a frontal assault but locked the gorge shut with crossbowmen and patrolled the roads with horse, forcing the rebels to exhaust their stores inside the walls, while the rebels rode out to burn court baggage carts and strike at Hanzhong in the hope of gaining time. Military pressure and inducement ran in parallel, for the rebel force held conflicting interests between local great families and displaced people; the court kept the crossbow pressure on and at the same time sent word that surrender would preserve the villages while refusal meant no one would leave the city alive once it fell. In the end the rebel main body collapsed on the Shizhou line, the survivors scattered into the mountains, and the court was able to march on Chengdu. The rhythm of the whole campaign was less a single assault on walls than the work of three things together, the crossbow line, the lock-down of the road and the cutting of supply, which between them drove the opponent into a place where he could not stand.
data: 可核對的數字有限，先列確定部分：北周大象二年，即公元五百八十；事發在九月；戰場在益州始州，即今四川廣漢一帶，經度約一百零四點二八度、緯度約三十點九八度。劍門關在始州以北，關道自北而南沿沱水谷地展開，自利州至始州一段山道，關與城相距數十至百餘里，谷道寬處可容馬車並行，窄處僅容一馬一車，攻守任何一方失去兩翼控制即等於全線崩解。弩的數字也大致可推：弩的有效射程通常在一百步上下，強弩可及二百步，射程與精度都勝過常見的角弓；單兵蹶張弩裝填的時間長過拉弓，但每名射手可連續發射數十箭，一列弩手齊射形成的覆蓋面，是壓制城頭最有效的手段。兵員方面，傳記只說叛軍聚眾為亂、人數以萬計，未載確數；官軍出蜀的兵眾與分道，諸書亦不載實數，只知主力由楊堅親領，別有守漢中、督漕之兵。糧秣可以估算的只是量級：入蜀山路一夫一牛所負有限，數百里山程的運輸須以萬計的車牛與舟船輪番接力，漢中屯田與成都平原的稻米構成了兩軍共同的底子。記載本身的稀疏更值得留意：此役的戰報、斬獲數與雙方損耗數，現存史籍皆無完整記載，各書所記互有出入，諸說並存。
dataEn: The numbers that can be checked are few, so begin with what is certain: the second year of Daxiang in Northern Zhou, that is AD 580; the rising began in September; the battlefield was at Shizhou in Yizhou, in the neighbourhood of present-day Guanghan in Sichuan, at roughly 104.28 degrees east and 30.98 degrees north. Jianmen Pass lies north of Shizhou, and the road of the pass runs north to south along the valley of the Tuo, so that the stretch from Lizhou to Shizhou runs from several tens to more than a hundred li; in the wider parts of the gorge cart and horse can pass abreast, in the narrow parts only one horse and one cart fit, and for either side the loss of the flanking heights means the collapse of the whole line. The figures for the crossbow can be roughly inferred as well: the effective range of a crossbow is normally around a hundred paces, a strong crossbow reaches two hundred, and both range and accuracy exceed what an ordinary recurve can do; reloading the single-man treading crossbow takes longer than drawing a bow, but each shooter can loose dozens of shafts in succession, and the sheet of bolts thrown by a rank of crossbowmen is the most effective way to hold down a city wall. On strength, the records only say that the rebels raised a mass of men numbered in thousands and give no exact figure; the size of the court column that marched into Shu and the roads it marched by are likewise without exact numbers in the histories, all that is known being that the main body was led by Yang Jian in person, with other troops told off to hold Hanzhong and to supervise the river transport. For supply only the order of magnitude can be estimated: on the mountain roads a man and an ox can carry very little, so a march of several hundred li required relays of carts, oxen and boats in their thousands, and the rice of the Chengdu plain together with the tuntian of Hanzhong formed the common basis of both armies. The sparseness of the record deserves note in itself: the reports, the numbers taken and the losses on both sides are not preserved in any complete form in the surviving histories, and what the different books say differs and stands side by side without resolution.
cause: 起事有遠因，也有近因。遠因是蜀地長久的治理失衡：益州自漢晉以來是南方財賦重地，稻米、錦彩、鹽鐵之利甲於天下，州郡之中豪右勢力雄厚，刺史往往倚之為爪牙，朝廷徵發兵糧既費時日，又容易激起地方反感。近因是北周末年的兵禍連綿：大象元、二年之間，朝廷先平幷州之亂，四月又平鄴城尉遲迥之亂，關中、荊襄的府兵與民夫屢次被抽調，田疇失耕、戶口流散；蜀中徵發的丁壯與糧賦加派，怨望積聚。九月，益州人李嚴聚眾為亂，眾以萬計，一鼓攻入成都，刺史不能守，郡縣望風響應者數十，叛軍以山川險固為巢，聲勢很快蔓延到梁州。直接導火線的具體經過，史無完整記載，事後追論多歸於豪右爭地與朝廷括戶逼民之爭，也有人以為與蜀中局部水旱相涉，但這些都屬推測，不能視為定論。朝廷的反應則明確：蜀地不可久失，而北方新平、兵未全復，遂授楊堅帥師入蜀，指望速戰速決。同一時間，南方陳朝正逢宣帝崩、太子即位，江南自顧不暇，只能隔著秦嶺袖手旁觀，遂令蜀地亂局延續數月。
causeEn: The rising had distant causes as well as immediate ones. The distant cause was the long failure of government in Shu: since Han and Jin times Yizhou had been a rich southern province, with rice, silk, salt and iron unsurpassed in the south, and within the commanderies the local great families were powerful, the governors leaning on them as instruments; the court's levies of men and grain were slow to organise and constantly risked arousing local resentment. The immediate cause was the unbroken run of wars at the end of Zhou: between the first and second years of Daxiang the court had put down the rising in Bingzhou and, in April, the revolt of Wei Chi-chiong at Yecheng, and the household troops and corvée of Guanzhong and Jingxiang were drawn out again and again, leaving fields untilled and households adrift, while the draft of labour and the additional grain levies in Shu piled up grievance. In September Li Yan of Yizhou raised a mass of men numbered in thousands, broke into Chengdu in a single rush, and the governor could not hold the city; dozens of commanderies answered the call, the rebels made the mountains their nest, and the disturbance spread quickly into Liangzhou. The precise course of the spark is not preserved: later argument has put it variously on the struggle of the great families for land and on the court's registration and exactions pressing the people, and some have linked it to local flood or drought, but these are inferences and cannot be treated as settled. The court's response, by contrast, is clear: Shu could not be left long in disorder, while in the north the recent wars were only just over and the troops not yet rested, so the command was given to Yang Jian to march into Shu with the hope of ending the matter quickly. At the same time the Chen court in the south was dealing with the death of Emperor Xuan and the accession of the crown prince, and had no room to look away from its own affairs; it could only watch from beyond the Qinling, which allowed the disorder in Shu to run for several months.
impact: 此役結束後，北周對西南的控制在最後階段重新合攏，益州、梁州各郡縣復歸朝廷版籍，叛軍殘部散入山澤，州郡秩序的重建成為隋朝接管蜀地的第一件事，而這件事日後由隋文帝楊堅親手推動。從大局面看，一場蜀中的地方叛亂把北周末年最後的內部裂痕暴露在長距離戰線的另一端，也襯出關隴軍制在承平之後的效率：兵精糧足而不難越劍門，壞在守方沒有可倚的關防與後援。北周旋為隋所代（五百八十一年），開皇之後的編戶齊民、租調輸運，無不以此局為基。制度層面，弩在南北朝已是受管制的軍資，隋唐律「私有禁兵器」條把甲、弩一併列為禁物，意味著這場仗裡大量消耗的弩機與弩矢，事後必須收繳登記、編入官庫軍簿，民間私藏的弩件也要收繳。蜀地在隋朝則轉為屯田與調運的基地，稻米、錦彩與山地物資沿沱水、嘉陵水持續北運，供應洛陽與長安，蜀地與中原的物質連結反而比戰前更為制度化。對陳朝而言，蜀中指望落空，北方門戶反而更近，五年之後的滅國之局已在暗中成形。
impactEn: When the campaign ended, Northern Zhou's control of the southwest closed up again in its final stage: the commanderies of Yizhou and Liangzhou returned to the court's registers, the remnants of the rebel force scattered into the mountains, and the rebuilding of order in the commanderies became the first task of the Sui in taking over Shu, a task that Yang Jian as Sui Wendi later carried out in person. Seen from the larger angle, a local rising in Shu exposed the last internal fractures of late Zhou at the far end of a long line of communication, and at the same time it showed what the Guanzhong military system could still do after a long peace: it was not hard for such an army, well found and well supplied, to cross Jianmen, and the failure lay with the defenders, who had neither defensible passes nor relief to fall back on. Zhou was then replaced by Sui in AD 581. On the institutional level, the crossbow had already become regulated matériel by the Northern and Southern dynasties, and the article on privately owned forbidden weapons in the Sui and Tang codes listed armour and crossbows together as prohibited, which meant that the locks and bolts consumed in this campaign had afterwards to be collected, registered and entered in the government stores and rolls, while the pieces privately kept by households were confiscated as well. Shu in the Sui period became a base of tuntian and transport, its rice, silk and mountain produce moving north along the Tuo and the Jialing to feed Luoyang and Chang'an, so that the material tie between Shu and the Central Plain became more systematised after the war than before it. For Chen the hopes set on Shu came to nothing while the door in the north stood nearer than ever, and the shape of the state's destruction five years later was already forming in the dark.
result: 結果是官軍平定了益州叛亂，始州以下的蜀道重開，楊堅得以率師入成都，益州與梁州各郡縣重新歸順北周朝廷，李嚴的下落則各書記載不一，或云兵敗請降，或云西走為流寇，後世無從核實，這也說明此役的當時記錄本身極為有限。可以確定的是，叛亂始於九月，平定在同年秋冬之交，北周由此避免了西南方向出現第二個尉遲迥式的割據；楊堅平蜀之功與平鄴之功相疊，使他在北周的權力再無對手，五百八十一年受禪建隋已是水到渠成。對地方而言，蜀地經歷兵亂、徭役與反覆徵發，人口與土地都需要重新編訂，州縣官員、戶籍與屯田的整頓延續到隋朝初年才見粗定；陳朝在此期間贏得了喘息，卻沒有恢復實力，南北對峙的均勢反而被推向外強中乾的一端。若以兵器來看，這場仗留下的最實在的遺產不是城池，而是弩的用法：弩陣在谷道中的部署、弩砲在城頭的架設，以及弩手與步騎的交替進擊，後來成為隋唐城防與山地作戰的常規，而弩本身也從消耗品變成了受官府編管的禁物，這一轉變正是在這條劍門谷道之後逐步完成的。
resultEn: The outcome was that the court suppressed the rising in Yizhou, the road below Shizhou reopened, Yang Jian was able to lead his army into Chengdu, and the commanderies of Yizhou and Liangzhou returned to their allegiance to the Zhou court. Li Yan's fate is reported differently from book to book, some saying that he surrendered after his defeat, others that he fled west as a bandit, and later ages cannot settle it, which is itself a measure of how thin the contemporary record of this campaign is. What can be fixed is that the rising began in September, that it was settled by the turn of autumn and winter in the same year, and that Zhou thus avoided a second Wei Chi-chiong-style secession in the southwest. Yang Jian's credit for pacifying Shu, laid on top of his credit for Yecheng, left him without a rival in the state, and the transfer of the throne to found the Sui in AD 581 was the natural conclusion of that. Locally, Shu had passed through war, corvée and repeated levies, so that population and land both needed to be re-registered, and the work of setting the commanderies right, registering households and reorganising the tuntian dragged on into the first years of the Sui before anything like a settled order appeared. Chen gained a breathing space in the same months but recovered no real strength, and the balance between north and south was pushed further toward a north that looked strong from outside and hollow within. In terms of weapons, the most solid inheritance of this war was not a city but a way of using the crossbow: the deployment of crossbow lines in a valley, the mounting of crossbow engines on a city wall, and the alternation of crossbowmen with foot and horse in the assault all became regular practice in Sui and Tang fortification and mountain fighting, while the crossbow itself moved from being a consumable to being materiel registered by the government, a change that was worked out step by step after this road through the Jianmen gorge.
